summary.headline: D.P. Abhushan Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87% YoY to INR1,338.9 crore, with PAT up 101% to INR50.6 crore; FY26 PAT INR211.8 crore (+88%).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,338.9 crore (+87% YoY), EBITDA INR73 crore (+72%, margin 5.45%) and PAT INR50.6 crore (+101%, margin 3.78%). For FY26, revenue grew 23% to INR4,070.3 crore, EBITDA rose 77% to INR309.7 crore (margin 7.61%, +234 bps) and PAT rose 88% to INR211.8 crore (margin 5.20%, +180 bps). Growth was mainly value-led, with volumes down about 20% per management. The QIP has been put on hold due to market conditions, and expansion has been slowed to 5-6 stores in FY27 from earlier guidance.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in full-year terms; diamond declined ~5% YoY

segments.name: Gold
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 gold revenue grew ~80% YoY and was the primary growth driver; FY26 gold revenue was INR3,702 crore (+~21%).

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 silver revenue rose from INR16 crore to INR69 crore (~+333%); FY26 silver revenue INR183 crore (from INR68 crore, ~+168%).

segments.name: Diamond
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 diamond revenue rose ~38% YoY from INR26 crore to INR36 crore; FY26 diamond revenue fell ~5% YoY, which management linked to moderation in premium discretionary spend.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of around 20%+ targeted; management cites wedding demand and old gold exchange; FY27 revenue planned at ~INR4,800 crore and FY28 at ~INR5,500 crore (per Q&A).
EBITDA margin guidance of 6%-6.5% for FY27; gross margin expected at ~10%-11%.
FY30 EBITDA margin vision of 8%-8.5%, via product mix, hedging, GML and leasing, plus store maturity.
Long-term topline growth target of ~25%-30% annually through FY30 (by end-2030).
Store network target of ~51 stores by 2030; FY27 openings now 5-6 stores if conditions allow, possibly 3-4 on a conservative basis; some expansion may slip by one or two quarters.
Omni-channel to contribute 3%-5% of revenue over the next 3-5 years, with an incremental INR25-30 crore annual profit.
QIP on hold; equity raise of 5%-8% dilution considered later, with promoter holding post-dilution at ~65%-68% from ~75%.
Management says Q1 FY27 may beat the INR36 crore standalone profit from Q1 FY25 ("We are trying").
capex_capacity: Store network at 12 after Dhar opening in March 2026 (Ratlam expanded earlier in FY26); total retail area ~53,650 sq ft.
FY26 productivity: ~INR7.6 lakh revenue per sq ft and ~INR339 crore per store; average ticket size ~INR1.27 lakh; inventory turnover ~4.7x.
Inventory days rose to ~100 in FY26 from 87 in FY25, mainly due to stocking the Dhar store (INR100-125 crore lying with Dhar); management guides 75-85 (or 75-90) days normal.
New stores are typically 3,000-5,000 sq ft with INR40-60 crore minimum inventory each.
Expansion targets: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat (Dahod then Baroda), Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh; Jodhpur planned, Jaipur targeted in 1-2 years; one franchisee being onboarded as a pilot.
Funding: internal accruals, bank funding, and leasing/GML; no long-term borrowings planned; more than 90%-95% of the balance sheet is inventory.
demand_pricing: Product mix: wedding jewellery ~60%, festival and lightweight ~25%, corporate and gifting ~15%.
Store conversion stable at ~82%-83%; Ratlam and Ratlam II above average.
Same-store sales growth ~20% YoY per management; volumes down ~20% in FY26, so growth was value-led.
Old gold exchange is 35%-40% of sales; new stores (Ajmer, Neemuch, Ratlam, Dhar) contribute 12%-15% of the business.
April to mid-May demand described as good before the PM's comments on gold spending; management expects June-July to be seasonally weaker, with recovery from Raksha Bandhan.
Silver demand seen as intact and shifting from gold; the company is bullish across gold, diamond and silver.
Competition from Titan and Kalyan viewed as healthy; the company positions itself as a regional player with customer depth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin compression?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to gold price volatility from geopolitical factors; FY26 gross margin ~10% vs ~7.72% in FY25, up ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Will GML and hedging affect steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there may be a slight margin impact, but GML, futures and leasing should help working capital and gradually lower finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Demand in April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth was good in April and mid-May, before the PM's comments, with no pressure at showrooms and walk-ins continuing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY26 growth was volume versus value, and what was SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was mostly value-led; volumes fell ~20%; SSG ~20% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the FY26 and FY27 store and revenue guidance numbers revised down, and is the QIP the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is unchanged but the pace has slowed; some expansion may slip 1-2 quarters because of the PM's comments; long-term ~50-51 stores by 2030 remains.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory days at ~100 and what is normal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the spike to Dhar stocking in March; normal is 75-85 days, with 75-90 days as SOP; the company keeps higher inventory per store to drive turns.

qa_highlights.question: Funding and promoter holding after QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: QIP postponed, not cancelled; funding via internal accruals, bank lines, and leasing/GML; equity dilution 5%-8%, promoter holding to ~65%-68%.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility and hedging costs (GML, futures, leasing) that may weigh on margins and working capital.
Demand sensitivity after the PM's comments on gold spending; June-July seasonal softness; volume decline ~20% in FY26.
Diamond segment decline (~5% in FY26) against management's margin expansion assumption.
Operating cash flow remains weak because inventory rises with each store; inventory days ~100 at FY26 end.
QIP on hold; FY27 store openings may be cut to 3-4; monitor delivery against 25%-30% growth target.
Franchise model is at pilot stage; omni-channel contribution and the INR25-30 crore profit target are unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and margin targets, but cautious on near-term demand; management slowed store expansion, deferred the QIP and framed the PM's remarks as a short-term sentiment risk. Answers on inventory and margin were detailed but some targets (volume, SSG, Q1 FY27 profit) were stated without supporting data.
key_quotes: Rising gold prices have pushed consumers toward lighter designs.

For us, it helps build a forward -booked demand pipeline with strong customer lock -in and assured conversion into jewellery sales, thereby improving visibility and supporting demand stability in a high gold price scenario.
So, we are targeting EBITDA margins to remain between 8% and 8.5%, which is our FY30 vision already in place.

adds.what: Store additions FY27: 5-6 stores (possibly 3-4 on conservative basis); store network 12 after Dhar opening March 2026, target ~51 stores by 2030

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of ~20%+ (INR4,800 crore planned) backed by 5-6 new stores (possibly 3-4) and wedding demand, but volumes fell ~20% in FY26 so growth is value-led, the QIP is on hold and some expansion may slip 1-2 quarters.
